observations.question: Why did the API return HTTP 503 after deployment?
observations.answer: The API returned HTTP 503 after deployment because PostgreSQL connections were exhausted. The team reduced the application connection pool to 20 and closed leaked connections, which resolved the issue without requiring a database restart. [S1]

observations.question: What does AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED mean?
observations.answer: AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED means the access token exceeded its expiry time. Obtain a new access token using the approved login flow. [S1]

citations.excerpt:
# Token recovery

AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED means the access token exceeded its expiry time. Obtain a new access token using the approved login flow. Never disable issuer or audience validation.

observations.question: Compare PostgreSQL connection pool limits in runbooks A and B.
observations.answer: Runbook A specifies a maximum PostgreSQL connection pool size of 10 per application instance, while Runbook B specifies a maximum of 20 per application instance. The database failure postmortem indicates that reducing the application connection pool to 20 resolved connection exhaustion issues. [S1] [S2] [S3]
